## The problem

Taking a feature-complete app through store compliance, asset size and multiplayer reliability to a releasable build.

## Approach

Versioned release checklists and a data-safety inventory; scripted PNG to WebP asset migration; seeded deterministic combat with an append-only Firestore action log enabling replay; mission, placement and clearance validators.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Shows disciplined delivery: measured optimization, compliance tracking and auditable state.
:::

## Results

| Result | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Assets reduced 72.3 MB to 6.3 MB via WebP | git blob sums of public/assets: 72.3 MiB at ee1c5cd^ to 6.1 MiB at ee1c5cd; du now 6.3M; scripts/optimize-assets.mjs |
| All 19 campaign missions pass validation | npm run validate run 2026-09-17: missions and placements clean; clearance 1 cosmetic warning |
| PWA precache 77 MB to 8.98 MB | CHANGELOG 1.4.13; not rebuilt |

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- Not publicly listed; 1.4.13 AAB not built
- No unit/integration test framework; QA is validators plus manual smoke tests
- FCM Cloud Function deploy and live push unverified
- No remote backup of repo or keystore

## Tools

JavaScript, Phaser 3, Vite, Capacitor 8, Firebase Auth, Firestore, Cloud Functions, FCM, Android
